lessons.title: Thought groups
lessons.explain: Break long sentences into short meaning groups with a tiny pause between them. It sounds calm and clear.
points: Never pause in the middle of a thought group.

items.text: When I got home, I realized I had forgotten my keys.
items.pattern: When I got home / I realized / I had forgotten my keys.

items.text: In my opinion, learning a language takes time and patience.
items.pattern: In my opinion / learning a language / takes time and patience.

items.text: If you have any questions, please let me know.
items.pattern: If you have any questions / please let me know.

lessons.title: Breath groups for longer answers
lessons.explain: In a two-minute answer, plan where you breathe. Breathe at the end of a group, never in the middle of one.
points: Drop your pitch slightly at the end of a completed group.

items.text: The place I'd like to talk about is a small café near my old apartment, which I visited almost every weekend.
items.pattern: The place I'd like to talk about / is a small café near my old apartment / which I visited almost every weekend.

items.text: I started learning English at school, but I only became confident when I began speaking every day.
items.pattern: I started learning English at school / but I only became confident / when I began speaking every day.

lessons.title: Chunking when giving directions
lessons.explain: Direction-giving is much easier to follow when broken into small chunks with pauses.

items.text: Go straight ahead, then turn left at the second light, and it's on your right.
items.pattern: Go straight ahead / then turn left at the second light / and it's on your right.

lessons.title: Chunking in a presentation opening
lessons.explain: Presentations sound much more confident when chunked clearly, giving the audience time to process.

items.text: Good morning everyone, thank you for coming, and let's get started.
items.pattern: Good morning everyone / thank you for coming / and let's get started.

lessons.title: Chunking in storytelling
lessons.explain: Stories flow better and build suspense when chunked at natural narrative breaks.

items.text: So one day, I was walking home from work, when I suddenly heard a strange noise behind me.
items.pattern: So one day / I was walking home from work / when I suddenly heard a strange noise behind me.

lessons.title: Chunking in IELTS-style long answers
lessons.explain: For Part 2 or Part 3 answers, chunk each supporting reason separately so the examiner can follow your structure.

items.text: I think remote work has both advantages and disadvantages, because on one hand it gives people more flexibility, but on the other hand it can make teamwork harder.
items.pattern: I think remote work has both advantages and disadvantages / because on one hand it gives people more flexibility / but on the other hand it can make teamwork harder.

lessons.title: Chunking with introductory phrases
lessons.explain: A short introductory phrase is usually its own chunk, set off with a small pause.

items.text: Honestly, I don't really mind either way.
items.pattern: Honestly / I don't really mind either way.

items.text: To be fair, he did apologize afterwards.
items.pattern: To be fair / he did apologize afterwards.

lessons.title: Chunking a recipe
lessons.explain: Recipe steps naturally break into chunks at each action — pause briefly between them.

items.text: First, chop the onions, then fry them in a little oil, and add the garlic once they're soft.
items.pattern: First, chop the onions / then fry them in a little oil / and add the garlic once they're soft.

lessons.title: Chunking when comparing two things
lessons.explain: Comparisons chunk around each side of the comparison, with a small pause before the contrast word.

items.text: Living in the city is more convenient, but living in the countryside is much more peaceful.
items.pattern: Living in the city is more convenient / but living in the countryside is much more peaceful.

lessons.title: Chunking while describing a chart or graph
lessons.explain: Describing data chunks around each trend or figure, giving the listener time to picture it.

items.text: The graph shows a steady increase from 2010 to 2015, followed by a sharp drop in 2016.
items.pattern: The graph shows a steady increase from 2010 to 2015 / followed by a sharp drop in 2016.

lessons.title: Chunking a formal message read aloud
lessons.explain: Reading a formal email or message aloud still needs natural chunking, not a flat word-by-word read.

items.text: Dear team, I wanted to let you know that the meeting has been moved to Thursday at 3pm.
items.pattern: Dear team / I wanted to let you know / that the meeting has been moved to Thursday at 3pm.

lessons.title: Chunking sentences with relative clauses
lessons.explain: A relative clause ('which...', 'who...') is usually its own chunk, set off by small pauses on both sides.

items.text: My brother, who lives in Canada, is visiting next month.
items.pattern: My brother / who lives in Canada / is visiting next month.

lessons.title: Chunking safety instructions
lessons.explain: Safety instructions need very clear chunking so each instruction is unmistakable.

items.text: In case of fire, stay calm, leave the building immediately, and do not use the elevator.
items.pattern: In case of fire / stay calm / leave the building immediately / and do not use the elevator.

lessons.title: Chunking practice: sentences that keep growing
lessons.explain: As a sentence grows longer, the number of chunks grows too — practise adding one chunk at a time.

items.text: I like coffee.
items.pattern: 1 chunk

items.text: I like coffee, especially in the morning.
items.pattern: 2 chunks

items.text: I like coffee, especially in the morning, when I need to wake up properly.
items.pattern: 3 chunks

lessons.title: Chunking in a job interview answer
lessons.explain: Structured interview answers chunk around each part of the story: situation, action, result.

items.text: In my last role, we had a tight deadline, so I reorganized the team's priorities, and we ended up delivering two days early.
items.pattern: In my last role, we had a tight deadline / so I reorganized the team's priorities / and we ended up delivering two days early.

lessons.title: Chunking parenthetical asides
lessons.explain: An extra comment inserted mid-sentence is its own chunk, set off clearly on both sides.

items.text: My colleague, who's actually pretty new to the team, handled it really well.
items.pattern: My colleague / who's actually pretty new to the team / handled it really well.

lessons.title: Chunking 'not only... but also' structures
lessons.explain: Each half of this structure is its own chunk, with a small pause right before 'but also'.

items.text: Not only is it cheaper, but it's also much faster.
items.pattern: Not only is it cheaper / but it's also much faster.

lessons.title: Chunking a product demo
lessons.explain: Product demos chunk around each feature being shown, pausing to let it land before moving on.

items.text: So here you can see the dashboard, and if you click this button, it generates the report automatically.
items.pattern: So here you can see the dashboard / and if you click this button / it generates the report automatically.

lessons.title: Chunking when explaining rules of a game
lessons.explain: Rule explanations chunk around each individual rule so listeners can follow along.

items.text: Each player gets seven cards, and on your turn, you either play a card or draw a new one.
items.pattern: Each player gets seven cards / and on your turn / you either play a card or draw a new one.

lessons.title: Chunking with time clauses (before, after, while)
lessons.explain: Time clauses are usually their own chunk, whether they come at the start or end of the sentence.

items.text: Before you leave, make sure you lock the door.
items.pattern: Before you leave / make sure you lock the door.

items.text: I'll call you while I'm on my way there.
items.pattern: I'll call you / while I'm on my way there.

lessons.title: Chunking practice: even longer sentence buildup
lessons.explain: A second buildup drill, starting more complex and adding even more chunks.

items.text: I work in marketing.
items.pattern: 1 chunk

items.text: I work in marketing, mainly on social media campaigns.
items.pattern: 2 chunks

items.text: I work in marketing, mainly on social media campaigns, which I've been doing for about five years now.
items.pattern: 3 chunks

lessons.title: Chunking cause and effect
lessons.explain: Cause-and-effect sentences chunk around the cause and the resulting effect separately.

items.text: Because the flight was delayed, we missed our connection.
items.pattern: Because the flight was delayed / we missed our connection.

items.text: The store closed early, so we couldn't buy anything.
items.pattern: The store closed early / so we couldn't buy anything.

lessons.title: Chunking a list of pros and cons together
lessons.explain: When listing several pros and cons in one breath, each point gets its own small chunk.

items.text: It's affordable, it's convenient, but the quality isn't always consistent.
items.pattern: It's affordable / it's convenient / but the quality isn't always consistent.

lessons.title: Chunking a formal announcement at work
lessons.explain: Workplace announcements chunk clearly so nobody misses an important detail.

items.text: Starting next Monday, the office will be open until 7pm, so please plan your schedules accordingly.
items.pattern: Starting next Monday / the office will be open until 7pm / so please plan your schedules accordingly.

lessons.title: Chunking when telling someone bad news gently
lessons.explain: Delivering difficult news benefits from extra-clear chunking, giving the listener time to absorb each part.

items.text: I need to tell you something, and I want you to know it's not your fault, but the project's been cancelled.
items.pattern: I need to tell you something / and I want you to know it's not your fault / but the project's been cancelled.

lessons.title: Chunking a short tribute or toast
lessons.explain: A tribute speech chunks around each memory or quality being honoured, with a pause to let it land.

items.text: She's always been there for everyone, she never asks for anything in return, and today we get to celebrate her.
items.pattern: She's always been there for everyone / she never asks for anything in return / and today we get to celebrate her.

lessons.title: Chunking while describing a photo
lessons.explain: Describing an image chunks around each element you notice, moving from general to specific.

items.text: In this photo, there's a group of friends sitting by the lake, and you can tell they're having a great time.
items.pattern: In this photo / there's a group of friends sitting by the lake / and you can tell they're having a great time.

lessons.title: Chunking while explaining a historical event
lessons.explain: Historical explanations chunk around cause, event and consequence.

items.text: After years of tension, the two countries finally signed a peace agreement, which changed the region for decades.
items.pattern: After years of tension / the two countries finally signed a peace agreement / which changed the region for decades.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing a book or movie plot
lessons.explain: Plot summaries chunk around each major turning point in the story.

items.text: The main character starts out pretty naive, but after everything that happens, she ends up completely transformed.
items.pattern: The main character starts out pretty naive / but after everything that happens / she ends up completely transformed.

lessons.title: Chunking during a negotiation
lessons.explain: Negotiation chunks around your offer and your condition, giving weight to each part.

items.text: I could agree to that price, but only if we extend the deadline by two weeks.
items.pattern: I could agree to that price / but only if we extend the deadline by two weeks.

lessons.title: Chunking describing symptoms to a doctor
lessons.explain: Describing symptoms chunks around each separate symptom so nothing gets missed.

items.text: I've had a headache since yesterday, and this morning I also started feeling a bit dizzy.
items.pattern: I've had a headache since yesterday / and this morning I also started feeling a bit dizzy.

lessons.title: Chunking a travel itinerary
lessons.explain: Itineraries chunk around each day or destination.

items.text: We land on Monday, spend two days in the city, and then head to the coast for the weekend.
items.pattern: We land on Monday / spend two days in the city / and then head to the coast for the weekend.

lessons.title: Chunking while explaining a budget
lessons.explain: Budget explanations chunk around each category of spending.

items.text: Half of it goes to rent, a quarter goes to savings, and the rest covers everything else.
items.pattern: Half of it goes to rent / a quarter goes to savings / and the rest covers everything else.

lessons.title: Chunking while comparing job offers
lessons.explain: Comparing offers chunks around each job's pros, with a clear pause before the contrast.

items.text: The first offer pays more, but the second one has much better work-life balance.
items.pattern: The first offer pays more / but the second one has much better work-life balance.

lessons.title: Chunking while troubleshooting a problem
lessons.explain: Troubleshooting chunks around each thing you've already tried.

items.text: I've already restarted it twice, and I've also checked the cables, but it still won't turn on.
items.pattern: I've already restarted it twice / and I've also checked the cables / but it still won't turn on.

lessons.title: Chunking while narrating a dream
lessons.explain: Dream narration chunks around each strange or memorable moment.

items.text: I was walking through this huge house, and suddenly all the doors disappeared, and I just woke up.
items.pattern: I was walking through this huge house / and suddenly all the doors disappeared / and I just woke up.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing environmental issues
lessons.explain: Discussing environmental topics chunks around the problem and its consequence, common in IELTS Part 3.

items.text: As more forests are cut down, we lose important habitats, and that has a huge impact on biodiversity.
items.pattern: As more forests are cut down / we lose important habitats / and that has a huge impact on biodiversity.

lessons.title: Chunking while describing a city
lessons.explain: City descriptions chunk around each feature you mention.

items.text: It's a pretty small city, but it has a really nice old town, and the people are incredibly friendly.
items.pattern: It's a pretty small city / but it has a really nice old town / and the people are incredibly friendly.

lessons.title: Chunking while explaining a hobby in detail
lessons.explain: Hobby explanations chunk around what you do, why you enjoy it, and how often.

items.text: I've been into photography for a few years now, mostly landscapes, and I try to go out shooting every weekend.
items.pattern: I've been into photography for a few years now / mostly landscapes / and I try to go out shooting every weekend.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing childhood memories
lessons.explain: Nostalgic storytelling chunks around each remembered detail, common in IELTS Part 2.

items.text: Every summer we'd visit my grandparents' farm, and I remember waking up really early just to feed the animals.
items.pattern: Every summer we'd visit my grandparents' farm / and I remember waking up really early / just to feed the animals.

lessons.title: Chunking while explaining a company policy
lessons.explain: Policy explanations chunk around the rule and its exception or reasoning.

items.text: Employees can work remotely two days a week, as long as they're available for core meeting hours.
items.pattern: Employees can work remotely two days a week / as long as they're available for core meeting hours.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing exam or study strategies
lessons.explain: Study-strategy talk chunks around each technique being described.

items.text: I usually make flashcards for vocabulary, and then I review them right before bed, since that seems to help me remember better.
items.pattern: I usually make flashcards for vocabulary / and then I review them right before bed / since that seems to help me remember better.

lessons.title: Chunking while explaining an app feature
lessons.explain: Tech explanations chunk around each step or feature.

items.text: You just tap the plus icon, choose a category, and it automatically saves your entry.
items.pattern: You just tap the plus icon / choose a category / and it automatically saves your entry.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing sports highlights
lessons.explain: Sports recaps chunk around each key moment of the game.

items.text: They were down by ten points at halftime, but they made an incredible comeback in the final quarter.
items.pattern: They were down by ten points at halftime / but they made an incredible comeback in the final quarter.

lessons.title: Chunking while giving nutrition advice
lessons.explain: Health advice chunks around each recommendation.

items.text: Try to eat more vegetables, drink plenty of water, and avoid too much sugar in the evening.
items.pattern: Try to eat more vegetables / drink plenty of water / and avoid too much sugar in the evening.

lessons.title: Chunking while discussing weather patterns
lessons.explain: Weather-pattern discussion chunks around cause and typical result.

items.text: Because the city is near the coast, the weather changes really quickly, so it can be sunny one hour and rainy the next.
items.pattern: Because the city is near the coast / the weather changes really quickly / so it can be sunny one hour and rainy the next.

lessons.title: Chunking during a phone support call
lessons.explain: Support calls chunk around each troubleshooting step you ask the customer to try.

items.text: Okay, first can you check if it's plugged in properly, and then let me know what the screen shows.
items.pattern: Okay, first can you check if it's plugged in properly / and then let me know what the screen shows.

lessons.title: Chunking a short formal disclaimer
lessons.explain: Even dense formal text needs clear chunking when read aloud, or it becomes impossible to follow.

items.text: This offer is valid until the end of the month, applies only to new customers, and cannot be combined with other promotions.
items.pattern: This offer is valid until the end of the month / applies only to new customers / and cannot be combined with other promotions.

lessons.title: Chunking while weighing a personal decision
lessons.explain: Personal decision-making chunks around each factor being weighed, common in IELTS Part 3 discussion.

items.text: On one hand, staying here means job security, but on the other hand, moving abroad could open up a lot more opportunities.
items.pattern: On one hand, staying here means job security / but on the other hand, moving abroad could open up a lot more opportunities.

lessons.title: Final mixed chunking review
lessons.explain: A closing set — mark where you'd pause before checking the suggested chunks.

items.text: Even though it was raining, we decided to go for a walk anyway, since we hadn't seen each other in months.
items.pattern: Even though it was raining / we decided to go for a walk anyway / since we hadn't seen each other in months.
